summary: No region-specific signal was identified for Bretagne. The national assessment for France applies, and the full national layer is carried by the France record.
tangentialFactors: No source ranks Bretagne against other French regions on trans-specific incidents, complaints or enforcement, so no regional comparison can be drawn from the inventory.
localsOnly: No resident-facing legal, institutional or facility detail specific to Bretagne was identified. Prison placement, identity-document rules and the protection machinery available to trans residents of Bretagne operate under the national framework carried by the France record.
outOfScopeNotes:
The single source in the inventory, a BuzzFeed News feature of 12 January 2018 on transgender women in French prisons, documents the national prison-placement framework: Article D248 of the French Criminal Procedure Code requires men and women to be held in separate establishments, so trans women whose identity documents are marked male are placed in men's facilities, where the feature records threats of violence against them. The feature carries no Bretagne-specific detail, and the statement by Adeline Hazan, controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty, that transgender detainees suffer the most in prison is national in scope.

Whether any penitentiary establishment in Bretagne holds trans detainees in men's facilities or in isolation, and how those facilities respond to such cases, is not sourced in this inventory.
